title: Versioning prompts and tracking the effect of each change

videos.script: So far every version of the prompt has had a file of its own. A prompt in production lives in one file, and its past lives in git. {{log}} This lesson builds that past and reads it. Eight commits over two weeks of August, each with a line saying what changed. {{diff}} First you work out what a version actually is. The text is part of it. So are the settings, the model and the messages you judged it by. Change one of them and the answers move, even when the file does not. {{hot}} Then you run every commit against the same forty messages. One command prints a score and a token count for each. {{score}} Asking for JSON raised the score and lowered the cost. Two commits written for safety cost tokens and lost a message each on dev. And one, called make the examples easier to read, raised the score to twenty-seven. {{zero}} Three days later somebody put the examples back, and nobody ran the test set. By the end of the lesson you can see a change like that the same afternoon, before it is merged, with the names of the messages it broke. {{close}}
